tracks.title: Moon 2 (Roche Limit)
tracks.loreNote: The spark that ignited Ryan's solo orbit. A dark, aggressive rock track using the Roche limit to describe a toxic, fatal attraction, setting the high-friction, destructive tone for the rest of the record.

tracks.title: Fragmentation: Debris Field
tracks.loreNote: The moment the planet completely shatters. Bringing back the planetarium narrator, this track is a heavy, visceral explosion of distorted guitars and pounding drums representing the violent breaking of the terrestrial past.

tracks.title: Impact
tracks.loreNote: Transposes the terrestrial nightmare of the 1990 crash on I-81 into a cosmic collision. Driving 1980s hard rock describing Ryan's vessel being struck by a high-velocity fragment in the debris field.

tracks.title: Mayday: The Intercept
tracks.loreNote: Ryan intercepts the telemetry from Moon 1 and broadcasts a frantic distress signal. A massive 1980s arena rock anthem of survival as Cassidy arrives with the family to pull the broken Engine out of the dark.

tracks.title: Star City: Orbital Ward
tracks.loreNote: Transposes Ryan's grueling recovery at Star City General into an orbital medical bay. A brooding hard rock ballad that translates the strict survival routines of Protocol T-10 into starship maintenance.

tracks.title: The Anchor's Hold
tracks.loreNote: A massive 1980s power ballad detailing Ryan's early days of recovery. A tribute to Cassidy, leaning into the concept that her tight embrace is the only gravitational force keeping his fragmented pieces together.

tracks.title: The Penumbra: Transit
tracks.loreNote: The heavy-rock mirror to Cassidy's coldest solo track. Passing through the celestial shadow, Ryan fuses his driving 1980s hard rock with her signature analog synthesizers to face the dark together.

tracks.title: Artificial Gravity
tracks.loreNote: Set during the 'Stalemate Year' of 1991. A stripped-down, acoustic-driven rock track representing Ryan generating his own artificial gravity as he learns to play the guitar again under strict new physical limitations.

tracks.title: Friction: Reentry
tracks.loreNote: Drops the listener into the white-hot rage of the 1992 catastrophe. High-speed, aggressive hard rock that uses the superheated plasma of atmospheric re-entry as a direct metaphor for Julian Vance's corporate exploitation.

tracks.title: Twin Moons: Touchdown
tracks.loreNote: The epic Prog-Rock finale. The ultimate musical collision of the two siblings, fusing heavy distorted arena rock with sweeping analog synths. Ends with the Planetarium Narrator safely closing the 74-minute exhibition.
